task.description: Root-cause diagnosis of ISS-0418's continued recurrence AFTER the 2026-09-05 partial fix (Letflow.Engine.Wasm.InvocationLease, PR #927/e5d07019) shipped a concurrency cap wired into the isolated `mix test --only wasm_hang` subprocess's own tests. ISS-0418.yaml's own post-fix evidence (orch_note_20260905, recurrence_2026_09_05) shows the flake rate UNCHANGED (~50%, matching the pre-fix baseline within noise), meaning the concurrency-cap fix did not close the flake. Determine why, and recommend the next fix direction to CODE-DESIGNER.

result.note:
DIAGNOSIS: the 2026-09-05 partial fix targeted the WRONG dominant mechanism, and the codebase's own record already flagged this as a live, unrefuted possibility before I re-confirmed it here.

== What already shipped, confirmed by reading the code directly ==

`Letflow.Engine.Wasm.InvocationLease` (lib/letflow/engine/wasm/invocation_lease.ex) is a correctly-designed, monitor-backed counting semaphore. It IS wired into all 6 remaining `:wasm_hang`-tagged tests (test/letflow/engine/wasm/call_timeout_test.exs:88, host_api_write_test.exs:468, plugin_handler_test.exs:167/416/503/509) via `InvocationLease.try_acquire()`/`release/1` around each test's own hang dispatch. Its default cap is `max(div(System.schedulers_online(), 2), 1)` (invocation_lease.ex ~line 100). It is NOT wired into any production call site -- `Letflow.Engine.Wasm.PluginHandler.run_guest/3` and `Letflow.Engine.PluginInterface.invoke/2,3` are untouched, confirmed by grep (only test/ and the module's own file reference `InvocationLease`). This matches the module's own moduledoc, which states this plainly ("PRODUCTION WASM DISPATCH DOES NOT CALL THIS MODULE YET"). Production-dispatch integration is tracked as OQ-C (design doc iss0418-wasm-concurrency-cap.md, most plausibly REQ-056, still pending) and is NOT what is blocking CI -- CI only runs the isolated test subprocess.

== Why the cap does not fix the CI flake, confirmed by re-deriving the mechanism against real numbers ==

All three `:wasm_hang`-tagged test modules declare `use ExUnit.Case, async: false` (confirmed by grep). Combined with `lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check.test.ex`'s `run_wasm_hang_tests/0`, which runs a SINGLE `mix test --only wasm_hang` subprocess covering all 6 tagged tests together, ExUnit executes these tests ONE AT A TIME within one shared, long-lived BEAM node -- there is no genuine concurrent dispatch happening in this run at all. `InvocationLease`'s cap gates SIMULTANEOUS admission; with tests already serialized by ExUnit itself, the cap is never actually contended in this specific run (a `try_acquire`/`release` pair completes and frees its slot before the next test's `try_acquire` call ever runs). The cap was designed for, and correctly closes, a genuine BURST-of-concurrent-hangs threat model (relevant to a future production dispatch integration) -- it was never capable of fixing a purely SEQUENTIAL, cumulative depletion happening one test at a time in a single process lifetime, because nothing about that scenario ever exceeds the cap.

The actual mechanism is cumulative, monotonic leak accumulation within one BEAM node's lifetime: `wasmex`'s native `TOKIO_RUNTIME` worker-thread pool is sized to `available_parallelism()` at NIF-load time and never regrows (REQ-170 design doc §1.4, live-verified: a leaked thread is never reclaimed, confirmed again up to a 90s window by the 2026-09-05 design's own diagnosis). Counting distinct wasmex `Store`s (not raw dispatch lines, since design doc iss0418-wasm-concurrency-cap.md §6.1 row 1 makes 2 sequential calls against the SAME Store/pid, which is one leaked executor thread total, not two) across the current 6 tagged tests: call_timeout_test.exs 1 leak, host_api_write_test.exs 1 leak, plugin_handler_test.exs 4 leaks (rows 4, 6, and 2 in row 7 -- two separate `Wasmex.start_link/1` calls with different `timeout_ms` values) = 6 total leaked Stores accumulated, one at a time, inside ONE `mix test --only wasm_hang` OS process before it exits. `lib/letflow/design/iss0428-parallel-runner-in-check-test.md` line 41 records CI's own runner as effectively 2-vCPU-class ("a 2-vCPU host's budget"), meaning `available_parallelism()` and therefore the Tokio pool size on the actual CI runner is likely as small as ~2, not the 8 this dev host reports (`System.schedulers_online()` = 8 here, confirmed live). With a pool that small and 6 sequential, permanent leaks accumulating in one process, by roughly the 2nd-3rd hang test the pool is already exhausted; every subsequent hang test's OWN `Wasmex.start_link/1` or `Wasmex.call_function/4` call then has to wait for a free native worker thread that will never come free, hitting either ExUnit's per-test timeout or ExUnit's own start-instance hang -- exactly the two failure signatures ISS-0418.yaml's recurrence log already shows recurring (host_api_write_test.exs:460/461 ExUnit.TimeoutError in `start_instance` via `:proc_lib.sync_start/2`; call_timeout_test.exs:78/79 the same; plugin_handler_test.exs assertion-level failures pinned at the outer configured bound). No concurrency, real or apparent, is required for this to happen -- it is a pure ordering/cumulative-count problem, which is exactly why a concurrency cap left the failure rate statistically unchanged post-fix (ISS-0418.yaml orch_note_20260905: 2/4 post-fix attempts vs. a 3-in-6 pre-fix baseline, both ~50%; recurrence_2026_09_05: two more post-fix hits on the exact same two files/lines as every pre-fix recurrence). This IS the design doc's own previously-flagged, never-refuted 'sequential-exhaustion hypothesis' (iss0418-wasm-concurrency-cap.md §0 point 3, §6.0); I am now confirming it as the dominant mechanism rather than leaving it as an open alternative, based on the accumulated post-fix CI evidence already on file plus the async:false/single-subprocess mechanism trace above.

== Recommendation to CODE-DESIGNER ==

1. KEEP `Letflow.Engine.Wasm.InvocationLease` as-is. It is correctly designed for its actual stated purpose (bounding simultaneous burst blast-radius against real concurrent multi-tenant production traffic, once OQ-C's dispatch integration ships) and its own moduledoc already disclaims fixing cumulative long-run exhaustion. Do not modify its cap value, its config key, or its semantics to try to make it solve this CI flake -- no cap value can fix a problem that never exceeds the cap in the first place.

2. The structural fix for THIS flake is process-level isolation per leak, not an admission gate: change `lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check.test.ex`'s `run_wasm_hang_tests/0` so each `:wasm_hang`-tagged TEST runs in its OWN fresh `mix test <file>:<line> --only wasm_hang` subprocess (or equivalent per-test invocation), rather than one `mix test --only wasm_hang` subprocess covering all 6. Each subprocess gets a fresh BEAM node and therefore a fresh, unexhausted native Tokio pool (freshly loaded NIF, `available_parallelism()`-sized, zero prior leaks) -- a leaked thread then dies with that short-lived OS process before the NEXT test ever runs, exactly mirroring the isolation principle ISS-0352's own original fix already established one level up (isolating `:wasm_hang` from the main suite) but applied one level down (isolating each hang test from its sibling hang tests). This generalizes the 'subprocess-per-invocation isolation' option `InvocationLease`'s own moduledoc already names as an unbuilt follow-up (§4), at test-granularity rather than production-invocation-granularity, which is the granularity that actually matters here since this is a test-harness problem, not a production dispatch problem.

3. Per-FILE (not per-test) subprocess splitting is NOT sufficient on its own and should not be recommended as the fix: plugin_handler_test.exs alone accounts for 4 of the 6 leaked Stores (rows 4, 6, and 2 in row 7), which could still exceed a ~2-slot CI pool within that one file's subprocess. The design must isolate at the granularity of individual hang-dispatching tests (or, as a documented, narrower exception, keep row 7's own two-dispatch test body together since design doc §6.3.1 already argues that pair is irreducible within one test for its own AC4 ordering assertion -- at most 2 leaks in that one subprocess, which is safe even against a 2-slot pool).

4. Cost/tradeoff CODE-DESIGNER should size explicitly: this trades subprocess-startup overhead (BEAM boot + compile-manifest load, likely 1-3s per extra subprocess on CI) for reliability -- going from 1 subprocess to up to 6 adds meaningfully to `mix letflow.check.test`'s wall-clock time, but the current alternative (60-180s ExUnit timeouts recurring on ~50% of merges, per ISS-0418.yaml's own tally) is far more expensive in aggregate CI/agent time. State this tradeoff in the design rather than treating the added subprocess count as free.

5. Config/operator-configurability (task item (c) from the original handoff): no NEW config key is needed for this fix -- it is a pure test-harness restructuring inside `lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check.test.ex`, not a production runtime parameter. `InvocationLease`'s existing `Application.get_env(:letflow, :invocation_lease, [])[:cap]` config point remains the correct (and sufficient) operator-configurable surface for the SEPARATE, still-open production-dispatch-integration question (OQ-C) -- do not conflate the two.

6. Do NOT re-attempt further footprint reduction (fewer hang tests) as the primary fix -- ISS-0352's own resolution history already shows two rounds of that (9->7, then 8->6 dispatches) were each insufficient alone, and iss0418-wasm-concurrency-cap.md §6.3.1 already argues the remaining 6 are individually irreducible without deleting real coverage. Footprint reduction only lowers the number of subprocesses fewer subprocesses need to isolate; it does not substitute for isolating them.

7. Whether item (e) from the original handoff ('does the isolated wasm_hang subprocess need an explicit lower cap override') is now moot: yes, moot -- the subprocess-per-test restructuring in (2) makes the InvocationLease cap irrelevant to this flake's fix entirely (each subprocess dispatches at most 1-2 hangs, well under any plausible cap or pool size), so no separate CI-specific cap override is needed as part of this fix.
